messages:
maria: Heads up — automated blue/green swap to v2 in eu-west-1 started via GitOps but the canary is failing and the automation rolled back. Seeing readiness flaps on inference pods.

raj: Any logs yet? Could be the startupProbe or a resource request mismatch.

maria: Pasted the pod logs: 
```
2026-06-08T14:02:11Z ERROR model: init timed out after 15s
2026-06-08T14:02:12Z WARN kubelet: killing container due to liveness probe failure
```
Also found this in the helm values that went out with the release: 
```
startupProbe:
  failureThreshold: 1
  periodSeconds: 5
  timeoutSeconds: 15
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1
nodeSelector:
  gpu-type: a100
```

jess: Oof, timeoutSeconds=15 is way too low for model init on cold GPU nodes. Who changed the startupProbe?

kevin: That came from the PR that tried to speed up pod turnover. It looks like the GitOps repo's chart values were edited directly in the branch. Repo: https://git.redwood/inference/infra/helm-charts/compare/refs/heads/feature/fast-start

raj: Also noticed cluster-autoscaler didn't launch extra nodes — node pool is spot-backed and has taints preventing pods without the proper toleration. The new values added a nodeSelector so pods are being scheduled only on a100-labeled nodes, which are at capacity in eu-west-1.

alex: infra-sre ran `kubectl describe node` — shows 0 available GPUs on most nodes; a few nodes had GPU=0 reserved because a previous manual pool was created for batch jobs and has different labels. Looks like label drift.

maria: deploy-bot: Canary rollout v2 -> v1 auto-rollback executed at 14:08:27 due to unhealthy canary (45% error rate > threshold).

oncall-bot: Metric spike: https://grafana.redwood/d/abcd/inference-errors?orgId=1&from=now-30m - error rate peaked to 52% at 14:05 UTC.

jess: Short term mitigation: bump startupProbe timeout and failureThreshold in Helm values, and revert the nodeSelector change so scheduler can spread pods across more GPU nodes. Long term: change canary automation to slower steps.

kevin: Agreed. Also propose we tweak the progressive delivery policy in our canary controller: increase the stable window and lower the step increments. Current policy is `stableWindow: 1m, stepWeight: 20%`. Suggest `stableWindow: 3m, stepWeight: 5%`, and add `maxUnavailable: 1` so we don't shift too much at once. Example annotation for the GitOps chart: 
```
annotations:
  rollout.stableWindow: "3m"
  rollout.stepWeight: "5%"
  rollout.maxUnavailable: "1"
```

raj: There's also an infra cost angle — if we increase reserved GPU capacity in eu-west-1 to avoid scheduling issues we'll be paying for warm capacity. Finance flagged this last quarter. Can we try autoscaling first and only reserve if autoscaler can't keep up?

maria: I'm opening a hotfix PR to bump startupProbe to `timeoutSeconds: 90` and failureThreshold to `5`, plus revert the nodeSelector. PR: https://git.redwood/inference/infra/pulls/842. Will also add the rollout annotations mentioned by @kevin.

raj: We should import the manually-created node pool into Terraform to reconcile labels and avoid future drift. I'll start a terraform import + plan: 
```
terraform import module.eu-west1.node_pool.batch_pool projects/redwood/regions/eu-west1/nodePools/batch-pool
```

alex: After the hotfix applied, I manually scaled the a100 nodepool +2 nodes (on-call exception) to buy time. Monitor shows pods coming up on the new nodes but model init still slow until the GPU drivers finish loading.

maria: Quick test result: after patching startupProbe to 90s, second canary attempt progressed: 5% -> 10% -> stalled at 15% for 3m but error rate stayed within threshold. Automation decided to continue.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout resumed: weights 5%,10%,15% -> currently at 25% and climbing.

jess: Action items: 
- (maria) Hotfix PR merged, follow-up PR to add rollout policy defaults in chart.
- (raj) Import manual pools to Terraform and reconcile labels.
- (kevin) Update progressive delivery docs and default safe policy in ops repo.
- (alex) Re-evaluate autoscaler config for GPU pools (scale-up triggers + tolerations).

maria: Note for postmortem: automation rollback saved us from serving large volumes of errors, but the rollout was brittle because probes + nodeSelector + drifted node labels reduced scheduling choices. We'll keep canary automation but make it more conservative by default. :white_check_mark:

kevin: One more ops tweak: add a sanity check in the CI pipeline that validates helm values against a small set of runtime constraints (e.g., `startupProbe.timeoutSeconds >= 60` when `resources.limits.nvidia.com/gpu > 0`). That would have flagged this before the release.

raj: I'll follow up with a quick Terraform change and send a cost impact estimate for keeping +2 a100 nodes vs repeated cold starts.

maria: Thanks all — monitoring looks stable for now. Leaving the thread open for any late follow-ups.
